newsitem.title: RUSSIA: North Korea denies involvement in diplomat killing.
newsitem.headline: North Korea denies involvement in diplomat killing.

text.p: North Korea denied on Thursday that it was involved in the murder of South Korean consul Choi Duck-keun in the Russian far eastern city of Vladivostok on Tuesday night, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Asked to comment on Seoul media reports that North Korea might have been involved, Tass quoted a diplomat at the North Korean embassy in Moscow as saying: "Reports about this are nonsense, to which we pay no attention."
Choi was bludgeoned to death as he returned to his apartment in Vladivostok, a crime-ridden city seven time zones ahead of Moscow, tucked between China and the Sea of Japan.
The capital of Russia's Primorsk (Maritime) region has been dubbed Russia's "wild east" -- a frontier of capitalism bedevilled by turf battles between rival mafia gangs.
Russian foreign ministry spokesman Gennady Tarasov said Moscow had expressed its condolences to the South Korean embassy in Moscow and to the family of the slain diplomat.
"Measures are being taken to clarify all of the circumstances of the tragedy and find those who are guilty," Tarasov told a news briefing.
Tass said a senior Russian diplomat declined to speculate about any link between the murder and tension between North and South Korea. "I have absolutely no information on that."
Interfax news agency, in a report from Vladivostok, said local police were inclined to treat the killing as a domestic affair rather than the work of North Korean special forces.
"I think the special forces work more professionally," said Viktor Kondratov, head of the regional branch of the Federal Security Service (FSB)
Kondratov said it could have been a failed robbery attempt. "The Primorsk district is very criminal," he said.
South Korean media reports have suggested that North Korea was behind the murder in retaliation for South Korea's killing of the crew members of a North Korean submarine.
The North Korean diplomat told Tass that this version was "absolutely groundless".
Pyongyang has threatened to retaliate unless South Korea returns a submarine that intruded into the South two weeks ago, along with its surviving and dead crew.
The submarine landed an estimated 26 North Koreans. Twenty-two of them have been killed and one captured alive during a manhunt.

Asked about possible retaliation by Pyongyang, the diplomat said: "This will depend on the development of the situation and the position of the South Korean side in connection with our demands that the submarine and its crew be returned."

Interfax quoted a source in the Primorsk interior ministry as saying residents of the house in Vladivostok where the crime was committed reported seeing three people of Asian origin running out of the entrance.
Their appearance was similar to that of three people seen with the victim in a Korean restaurant one hour before the murder, the source said.

Russian FSB and interior ministry experts arrived in the region on Thursday to investigate possible motives for the attack, including personal vendetta, robbery or the possibility of a North Korean connection.
In Seoul, a foreign ministry spokesman said on Wednesday that Choi's wallet, passport, cash and other personal belongings were untouched, but there was a cut around his midriff.
